chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever finds something, it is for him; let him enjoy it until its claimant comes to him. When the claimant comes, he must return it to him.

key_terms.طَالِبُ: Claimant or seeker of the lost item

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on keeping and using found property before the owner is found?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the permissibility of temporary usufruct (*istimta'*) for the finder of lost property, distinguishing it from outright ownership. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the finder holds the item in trust until the owner claims it, ensuring the property is preserved and utilized without unjust enrichment.
